newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech RIF sees 1997 net down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Czech RIF sees 1997 net down sharply.

text.p: The largest Czech mutual fund Restitucni Investicni Fond (RIF) said on Friday that it expected 1997 net profit to fall to one billion crowns from its 2.26 billion crown net profit for 1996.
RIF board member Radek Micka told the fund's annunal general meeting that the forecast also assumes paying a gross dividend of between 50 to 80 crowns, down from 100 crowns this year.
"The amount of the 1997 dividend should be five to eight percent (of each share's nominal value of 1,000 crowns)," Micka said.
There was no immediate explanation for the drop in net profit .
The RIF fund was launched by the state-run National Property Fund culling three percent of the stock from companies privatised in the government's vouchers-for shares programme.
RIF shares are now publicly traded on the main market of the Prague Stock Exchange, but the NPF remains its primary shareholder.
